channel.title: The Shawnee News-Star - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from The Shawnee News-Star (news-star.com)

item.title: Agritourism grows nationwide, Census date shows riser income and wider reach
item.description: Agritourism continues to expand across the United States, providing new income opportunities for farmers while strengthening rural communities, according to data from the USDA’s 2022 Census of Agriculture.

item.title: Plan to build self-storage units on Union shut down
item.description: Shawnee City Commissioners denied a rezone request this month, shutting down plans to build personal storage/self-storage facilities by applicant Union Street Condominiums, LLC, c/o Johnson & Associates.

item.title: Former SHS wrestling coach Leen to be inducted into NJCAA Hall
item.description: The wrestling community has bestowed another honor on former Shawnee High School wrestling coach Mark Leen as he will be inducted into the National Junior College Athletic Association's Hall of Fame.

item.title: First United Bank hosts Harvesting Impact Competition to support ag programs, local nonprofits
item.description: SHAWNEE, OK — First United Bank recently wrapped up Harvesting Impact, a countywide competition designed to support agriculture programs across Pottawatomie County while connecting students with local nonprofit organizations addressing food insecurity.

item.title: Rezone proposal for abandoned nursing home site deferred
item.description: This month, a rezone request was brought before Shawnee City Commissioners regarding a former nursing home long abandoned at 1402 E. Independence, across the street from Sequoyah Elementary School; the item has been deferred.

item.title: Snow fun
item.description: This past week, as the Shawnee area and much of the state experienced a winter storm with plenty of snow accumulations, News-Star readers shared nearly 100 photos of outdoor winter fun, from snowball throws to sledding, and much more.

item.title: Gardens of the Cross Timbers: Gold mine in the kitchen
item.description: What a lingering winter storm. The days leading up to the event were hectic.

item.title: Shawnee Parks and Recreation
item.description: Hello Shawnee! Have you thawed out yet? The snow was very pretty, but it does cause many closures, delays, and slippery spots. We hope you stayed safe and warm! Be sure to keep an eye on the weather, as winter isn’t done yet.

item.title: OBU's MOSAIC event invites high school students to explore the arts
item.description: Oklahoma Baptist University’s Warren M. Angell School of Visual and Performing Arts invites high school students in grades 10–12 to campus for MOSAIC, an immersive arts experience to be held on April 8, 2026.
